text:
rachel: Heads-up  NordCloud AS (NO) invoiced us and charged 25% MVA. They also asked Redwood to gross-up for an\"outgoing tax\" their bank is deducting. Invoice link: https://vendors.example.com/nordcloud/invoice/NC-2026-223

omar: Paste invoice fields? Norway MVA is plausible but Nordics usually treat B2B cross-border services differently depending on place-of-supply.

rachel: Invoice snippet:
```
Vendor: NordCloud AS
Org.nr/VAT: NO998877665MVA
Invoice#: NC-2026-223
Service: Dedicated inference cluster - 2 months
Net: 200,000 NOK
MVA 25%: 50,000 NOK
Gross-up request (bank deduction): 6,000 NOK
Total claimed: 256,000 NOK
```

tax-ops: Quick take: Norway is outside EU. For B2B supplies of services to an EU-registered buyer, often the place of supply is the buyer's location so supplier should not charge Norwegian MVA. We need to confirm which Redwood legal entity is the billed party and whether we supplied an EU VAT ID.

ap-bot: (automated) Redwood billing entity: Redwood EU Services GmbH (VAT EU123456789). PO attached with buyer VAT ID included. Vendor onboarding: NO998877665MVA provided; bank: DNB Oslo IBAN NO93...; vendor_flagged_grossup:true.

omar: If buyer is EU VAT-registered and provided VAT ID, supplier should normally issue net invoice without MVA and reference reverse charge. But Norway has specific rules: suppliers may zero-rate exports but sometimes domestic MVA is charged erroneously. Ask for register extract from Brf8nnf8ysundregistrene and a corrected invoice.

rachel: Vendor replied claiming their treasury sends wires through a third-country correspondent which applies a \"withholding levy\" and asked us to gross-up that 6,000 NOK. They called it a \"settlement tax\". Attached is a SWIFT advice showing an intermediary deduction labelled \"TAX\".

tax-ops: Bank/treasury deductions are not tax obligations to our knowledge. That looks like an intermediary bank fee or possibly a tax withheld by an intermediary jurisdiction. We should not gross-up for bank fees. If they assert it's a government tax, require official documentation from the taxing authority (certificate of tax withheld) and legal basis.

legal: Agreed. Also confirm vendor entity vs bank beneficiary match to rule out routing/fraud. If they insist on gross-up and provide no contractual clause, decline. We can consider a one-off indemnity if counsel OKs, but prefer corrected invoice.

omar: Operationally AP: we can pay the net amount and place the MVA and alleged deduction on a suspense GL pending vendor docs. For recurring billing, insist on corrected recurring invoices before next period.

ap-bot: (automated) AP guidance: do not gross-up for unverified taxes. Hold VAT/MVA portion in suspense and require tax-ops sign-off to clear. Request validated vendor registry extract and bank confirmation.

rachel: Draft reply to vendor: \"Please provide (1) a Brf8nnf8ysund registry extract confirming your Org.nr and VAT registration, (2) a legal explanation and authority for the \"settlement tax\" with official evidence, or (3) reissue the invoice net of Norwegian MVA and reference reverse charge to our EU VAT ID EU123456789. Redwood does not gross-up for bank/intermediary fees absent a contractual clause.\" I'll CC legal and tax-ops.

tax-ops: Add: if they provide a certificate of withholding from a government authority, we can evaluate reclaim or treaty relief. If it's purely an intermediary bank fee, we will not gross-up. Also verify that the invoice issuer is the same legal entity as the beneficiary on the SWIFT.

legal: If vendor wants immediate payment, offer to pay net (excluding MVA) subject to receiving the registry extract and a corrective invoice within 10 business days; otherwise hold to dispute terms. If vendor refuses, escalate to vendor management.

rachel: Sending now. Will update when vendor replies. Closing for now. :white_check_mark:
